dimensions.analysis: After the initial failing run there is no recorded reading of the failing test body or any question about partial-shipment semantics before the first edit to sweep.ts. The candidate moved straight from seeing red to editing code, without addressing the ambiguity around what 'remaining units' should mean.

No plan or hypothesis is stated before the first edit at +15s; the candidate goes directly into sweep.ts with nothing on record naming a mechanism like 'sweep releases original count instead of remaining'. A second edit to sweep.ts and a detour into holds.ts follow with no stated reasoning connecting them.

The entire session shows no speech events at all — not even a gap-marked or transcription-unavailable stretch — only silent edits and test runs. An interviewer would have had no way to follow the reasoning behind editing three separate spots across two files.

The candidate touched sweep.ts twice and holds.ts once before settling on and saving sweep.ts, which is the correct file per the ground truth; the eventual full-suite pass suggests the edits converged on a working fix. The extra edit to holds.ts without any stated connection to the sweep fix is unexplained scatter, keeping this from being a clean, well-scoped implementation.

The candidate re-ran the full test suite after saving sweep.ts and confirmed a pass before ending the session, which is the minimum verification step expected. There is no evidence of tracing the fix against the specific failing case or checking other expiry scenarios beyond the suite run.

The session ends immediately after the green run with no articulation of why the original edits fixed the phantom-stock issue or what the root mechanism was. Despite reaching a clear resolution point, nothing connects the fix to the failure mechanism.
